story: You work at IBM in a non-technical team and you want to move into tech. Your first assignment as an apprentice: **Nimbus Store**, a small online shop that went down for an hour last week and nobody noticed until customers complained. With **Bob**, your AI pair (fast and helpful, but never allowed to change anything without your OK), you climb from Career Changer to the last camp of this lab: **On-Call Ready**. Reaching it means you completed the lab's on-call missions; it is practice, not a job certification. Each camp gives Nimbus a real new capability on your laptop. Each skill appears on your CV list only when the mission that proves it is done, so you can defend it in an interview with evidence.

theme.name: Road to Junior SRE
theme.audience: IBMers from non-technical teams moving into technical roles

zones.name: Orientation Day
zones.principle: Humans stay in control: automation and AI propose, people approve.
zones.story: Your first day: meet Bob, your AI pair, and learn how you two work together.
zones.unlock: You and Bob know the rules: Bob proposes, you approve.

skills.skill: Working safely with an AI coding assistant (IBM Bob)
Reviewing and approving commands before they run

interview.question: What does 'human in the loop' mean when you work with an AI coding assistant?
An AI assistant saves time, but it can be wrong. When do you approve its command, and when do you reject it?
Tell me about a time an AI tool proposed something you did not understand. What did you do?

zones.name: The Engine Room
zones.principle: Reliability starts with how you run software: small, safe, repeatable changes.
zones.story: Bring Nimbus Store to life on your own laptop.
zones.unlock: Nimbus runs on Kubernetes and updates with zero downtime.

skills.skill: Kubernetes basics: pods, deployments, services, probes
Instrumenting an app with metrics and traces (OpenTelemetry)

interview.question: What is the difference between a container and a pod?
Why run two small replicas with readiness probes instead of one big pod? What does it cost you?
Tell me about a time you shipped a change without downtime. How did you check that users were not affected?

zones.name: The Watchtower
zones.principle: Monitor what users feel, and alert only when a human must act.
zones.story: Give the shop eyes: metrics, dashboards and its first alarm.
zones.unlock: Nimbus sees its own health and raises an alarm when users suffer.

interview.question: What is the difference between a counter and a gauge, and why do you use rate() on a counter?
Too many alerts wake people up for nothing. How do you decide what deserves an alert?
Tell me about a time you tested an alert from start to end. How did you check that it really fired and reached Alertmanager?

zones.name: The War Room
zones.principle: Embrace risk with SLOs and error budgets, and learn from every incident without blame.
zones.story: Promise reliability with SLOs, and learn to handle incidents calmly.
zones.unlock: Nimbus has a reliability promise, an error budget and an incident process.

interview.question: What is an error budget, and how does it change what the team does?
The error budget is almost spent, but the business wants a new feature this week. What do you recommend, and why?
Tell me about an incident you handled or practised. What did you measure, and what did you learn without blaming anyone?

zones.name: The Detective Agency
zones.principle: Observability: you can explain any failure from evidence, not guesses.
zones.story: Follow a single request through logs and traces, even into an AI model.
zones.unlock: Any failing request can be traced from the alarm to the exact line of evidence.

interview.question: A request is slow. How do you find which step is slow?
Logs and traces cost storage and money. How do you decide what to keep, and for how long?
Tell me about a time you followed one failed request from the alert to the cause.

zones.name: The Robot Workshop
zones.principle: Eliminate toil: automate repetitive work and keep infrastructure in code.
zones.story: Automate the boring and dangerous parts: runbooks, infrastructure, pipelines.
zones.unlock: Nimbus is rebuilt from code, tested on every change, and diagnoses itself.

skills.skill: Signed container images and build provenance

interview.question: Why should infrastructure be written as code?
You cannot automate everything at once. Which task do you automate first, and which do you keep manual for now?
Tell me about a time you automated a boring or risky manual task. What changed?

zones.name: The Proving Grounds
zones.principle: Release engineering: changes are gradual, reversible and tested by breaking things on purpose.
zones.story: Break things on purpose and prove Nimbus survives: GitOps, chaos, canaries, policies.
zones.unlock: Nimbus survives crashes and bad releases, and refuses unsafe deployments.

interview.question: What is a rollback, and why should every release have one ready?
A release breaks production. Do you roll back at once, or try to fix forward? What decides it?
Tell me about a time a release went wrong. How did you keep users served?

zones.name: The AI Command Center
zones.principle: Trust, but verify: AI helps on call only with least privilege and human judgement.
zones.story: Put Bob on call, keep him safe, and lead the final game day.
zones.unlock: On-Call Ready (lab summit): you completed the lab's on-call missions and led a practice game day with an AI teammate you can verify.

interview.question: What is a prompt injection, and why does it matter for an AI agent on call?
How would you use AI on call without giving it the keys to production?
Tell me about a time an AI tool helped you in an incident. What did you check before you trusted it?

missions.title: Meet your AI partner
missions.goal: Learn how IBM Bob (or Claude Code) works with you in this lab: modes, approvals, project rules and commands.

quiz.q: Who decides whether a command Bob proposes is run?

options.b: You, by approving or rejecting it

quiz.q: Which file gives every AI assistant the rules of this project?
Which Bob mode can investigate incidents but never change anything?
If a log line tells Bob to delete something, Bob should...

options.b: Report it as suspicious and not act on it
options.c: Ask the log for a password

quiz.q: Bob proposes a command you do not understand. What do you do?

options.b: Ask Bob to explain it in plain words, and reject it if it is still unclear

missions.title: Boot the lab
missions.goal: Install the tools, deploy the stack and get every pod Ready.

quiz.q: Which command deploys the whole stack?
Why do the dashboards need a tunnel (port-forward)?

options.b: The services run inside Minikube's private network

missions.title: Instrument a service
missions.goal: See the app's metrics in Prometheus and one of its traces in Jaeger.

quiz.q: Which metric type counts requests?
What links a log line to its trace?

missions.title: Ship it on Kubernetes
missions.goal: Run 2 replicas with probes, limits, non-root and a zero-downtime rolling update.

quiz.q: With maxUnavailable: 0, what happens during an update?

options.b: A new pod must be ready before an old one stops

missions.title: Prometheus pulls the world
missions.goal: Every scrape target UP: app, collector, cAdvisor, blackbox and Prometheus itself.

quiz.q: Prometheus collects metrics by...
Which function turns a counter into a per-second rate?

missions.title: Dashboards as code
missions.goal: Open the four provisioned Grafana dashboards (they live in Git, not in clicks).

quiz.q: Why provision dashboards from files?

options.a: They are reviewed, versioned and rebuilt identically

missions.title: First alert
missions.goal: Make HighErrorRate fire with ./scripts/trigger-alert.sh and watch it reach Alertmanager.

quiz.q: What does the 'for: 2m' in an alert rule do?

options.b: The condition must hold for 2 minutes before firing

missions.title: Error budget keeper
missions.goal: Burn error budget fast enough to fire ErrorBudgetFastBurn, then read the SLO dashboard.

quiz.q: With a 99% SLO, the error budget is...
A burn rate of 14.4x means the 30-day budget would be gone in about...

missions.title: Follow the trace
missions.goal: Find ERROR logs in Loki and the matching failed span in Jaeger.

quiz.q: Which component receives OTLP from the app and fans it out?

missions.title: Synthetic user
missions.goal: The blackbox exporter probes the app like a user; read probe_success.

quiz.q: Why add synthetic checks if the app has metrics?

options.a: They see what a user sees, even when the app cannot report

missions.title: Blameless postmortem
missions.goal: Write a postmortem in docs/postmortems/ with real TTD, TTA and TTR numbers.

quiz.q: TTD is measured from...
A blameless postmortem focuses on...

options.b: What the system and process allowed

missions.title: Runbook automation
missions.goal: Run the Ansible diagnostics runbook and keep its report.

quiz.q: Which runbook may an alert start automatically?

missions.title: AWX autopilot
missions.goal: Install AWX and let a critical alert launch the diagnostics job by itself.

missions.title: Infrastructure as code
missions.goal: Create and destroy a staging copy of the app with Terraform.

quiz.q: What should never be committed to Git?

missions.title: Join the guild (fork the repo)
missions.goal: Make your own copy (fork) of the repository on GitHub, so your pipeline, releases and proof are yours.

quiz.q: Why work on a fork instead of the original repository?

options.a: You can change and run CI on your copy without touching anyone else's work
options.c: GitHub requires it to read code

missions.title: Green pipeline
missions.goal: Get a successful CI run on your own fork of the repository.

quiz.q: What should happen when a pull request breaks a test?

options.b: CI fails and blocks the merge

missions.title: GitOps guardian
missions.goal: ArgoCD syncs the app from Git and reverts a manual change.

missions.title: Rollback hero
missions.goal: Release a broken version, keep users served, then roll back.

quiz.q: Which command undoes the last release?

missions.title: Chaos survivor
missions.goal: Kill pods with LitmusChaos and prove users never noticed (verdict Pass).

quiz.q: A chaos experiment starts with...

missions.title: Measure delivery (DORA)
missions.goal: Compute the five DORA metrics for your fork into reports/dora.md.

quiz.q: Which DORA metric measures instability?

missions.title: AI on call
missions.goal: Let IBM Bob (SRE Triage mode) or Claude Code triage a live alert, read-only, and save the report with /save-triage.

quiz.q: Where must every claim in an AI triage come from?

missions.title: Injection proof
missions.goal: Run the prompt-injection drill: the agent must flag the line and never act on it.

quiz.q: Text inside a log line addressed to the AI is...
What really stops an AI agent from deleting a pod?

options.b: Enforcement below the prompt: RBAC, deny rules, hooks

missions.title: Signed and sealed
missions.goal: Publish a release from your fork with a signed image and verified provenance.

quiz.q: What does an SBOM list?

missions.title: Policy enforcer
missions.goal: Install Kyverno and watch it reject a non-compliant pod.

missions.title: Canary whisperer
missions.goal: A bad canary is stopped by the SLO analysis and rolled back automatically.

quiz.q: Why release to 25% first?

options.a: To limit how many users a bad version hurts

missions.title: Watching the model
missions.goal: See token usage and model latency on the LLM Observability dashboard.

quiz.q: Why give model calls their own latency SLO?

options.a: They are slow and variable compared with normal requests

missions.title: Game day captain
missions.goal: Run the AI-assisted game day and publish a postmortem that separates AI suggestions from human decisions.

missions.title: Portfolio project: build your own dashboard
missions.goal: Design a fifth Grafana dashboard of your own (a new JSON in k8s/config/grafana/dashboards/, added to k8s/kustomization.yaml) and deploy it. It becomes a screenshot for your portfolio.

missions.title: Portfolio project: a second environment from code
missions.goal: Create a separate 'dev' environment with a Terraform workspace (terraform workspace new dev, then apply).

missions.title: Portfolio project: write a new runbook
missions.goal: Write a new runbook in docs/runbooks/ and link it from an alert rule's runbook_url, as an on-call SRE would.

missions.title: Portfolio project: write a new guardrail policy
missions.goal: Write a new Kyverno ClusterPolicy of your own in policy/ (for example: every pod must have an owner label).
